items.title: The impact of martial arts-based interventions on cognitive function and motor performance in elementary school-aged children: a systematic review
items.venue: Pedagogy of Physical Culture and Sports

ai.headline: Martial arts may help children’s attention, self-control, balance and fitness, but are not proven better than other exercise.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 12 studies with about 1,300 children aged 6–12 found that martial arts programmes such as taekwondo and karate were linked to improvements in attention, self-regulation, balance, coordination and cardiorespiratory fitness. The evidence was mixed in quality and did not show martial arts are superior to other well-designed physical activity programmes.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that structured movement with rules and self-control can support skills useful in school and daily life, though more research is needed.
ai.life_skill: Try a structured activity that combines movement, balance and clear rules, such as a beginner martial arts class, and notice whether it helps your focus.
ai.fact: Martial arts-based interventions were linked to improvements in attention, self-regulation, balance, coordination and cardiorespiratory fitness in children aged 6–12.

quiz.question: What did the review find about martial arts compared with other physical activity programmes?
quiz.answer: It found possible benefits but did not establish that martial arts are superior to other well-designed physical activity programmes.

ai.caveat: The studies varied in methods and several had concerns or serious risk of bias, so the findings are not definitive proof.

items.title: Effects of Parent-Involved Digital Health Interventions on Adiposity-Related Outcomes and Behaviors in Children and Adolescents With Overweight or Obesity: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

ai.headline: Digital health programmes involving parents may slightly lower BMI in children and adolescents with overweight or obesity.
ai.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis looked at 29 randomised trials involving 4,156 children and adolescents with overweight or obesity. Parent-involved digital health interventions produced a small but statistically significant reduction in BMI-related outcomes compared with controls, though effects on diet, physical activity and sedentary behaviour were limited.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that involving parents through digital tools can support modest weight-related improvements in young people, but it is not a complete solution on its own.
ai.life_skill: Try involving a parent or caregiver when using a digital health app or programme to support healthier eating and activity habits.
ai.fact: Parent-involved digital health interventions were linked to a small reduction in BMI-related outcomes in children and adolescents with overweight or obesity.

quiz.question: What did parent-involved digital health interventions do to BMI-related outcomes compared with controls?
quiz.answer: They produced a small but statistically significant reduction in BMI-related outcomes.

ai.caveat: The evidence is moderate certainty, and the best digital delivery method or parent-involved strategy has not yet been established.

items.title: Systematic Review of the Association Between Sleep and Depression Among Korean Adolescents
items.venue: Asia-pacific Journal of Convergent Research Interchange

ai.headline: Poor sleep is linked to higher depressive symptoms in Korean adolescents.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at nine studies of Korean middle and high school students. It found that short sleep duration, poor sleep quality, insufficient sleep, insomnia, daytime sleepiness, later bedtime and evening chronotype were consistently linked to increased depressive symptoms.
ai.why_it_matters: Sleep habits may be an important part of adolescent mental health, though the review cannot show whether poor sleep causes depression.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your sleep patterns relate to your mood and consider speaking with a trusted adult or health professional if sleep problems persist.
ai.fact: Short sleep duration, poor sleep quality, insufficient sleep, insomnia, excessive daytime sleepiness, later bedtime and evening chronotype were consistently associated with increased depressive symptoms among Korean adolescents.

quiz.question: What did all nine studies in the review report about sleep-related factors and depression?
quiz.answer: All nine studies reported that at least one sleep-related factor was significantly associated with depression or depressive symptoms.

ai.caveat: The included studies were observational, so they show links rather than prove that sleep problems cause depression, and further longitudinal research is needed.

items.title: Living evidence map of the global climate and health literature.
items.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

ai.headline: Researchers are building a living map of global studies linking climate change and human health.
ai.summary: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review that plans to systematically map the worldwide literature on how climate change, weather, climate-forcing agents and fossil fuels relate to human health and well-being. It will be updated continuously and made searchable through an interactive interface.
ai.why_it_matters: It will help people see what research exists on climate-related health risks and where evidence is missing.
ai.life_skill: Check a trusted evidence map or health organisation for up-to-date information on climate-related health risks in your area.
ai.fact: Climate change, climate variability, weather, climate-forcing agents and fossil fuels are being studied for their links to human health and well-being.

quiz.question: What is the main aim of this Cochrane review?
quiz.answer: To systematically map the global literature on the relationship between climate-related factors and human health and well-being.

ai.caveat: This is only a protocol describing what the review plans to do, not a completed review with findings.

items.title: Infectious disease outbreaks among hospitalised neonates in low- and middle-income countries: a systematic review.

ai.headline: Drug-resistant Klebsiella bacteria cause most neonatal outbreaks in LMIC hospitals.
ai.summary: The review looked at 172 outbreaks in newborn units across 32 low- and middle-income countries. Gram-negative bacteria caused 74% of outbreaks, with Klebsiella spp. most common and often resistant to key antibiotics.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how antibiotic-resistant infections can spread in hospitals where newborns are cared for, highlighting why infection prevention matters worldwide.
ai.life_skill: Notice and ask about hand hygiene and cleaning practices when visiting healthcare settings.
ai.fact: Klebsiella spp. was the most frequently detected outbreak pathogen in neonatal units in LMICs.

quiz.question: What proportion of outbreaks were caused by Gram-negative bacteria?
quiz.answer: Gram-negative bacteria accounted for 74% of outbreaks.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and reporting deficiencies plus potential publication bias limited some analyses.

items.title: Models of Supportive Care for Parents of Infants in Neonatal Intensive Care Units: A Systematic Review of Their Characteristics and Outcome

ai.headline: Different supportive care models may help lower stress for parents of premature babies in neonatal intensive care.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 17 studies of supportive care models for parents with premature infants in NICUs. It identified six models, including family-centred care, kangaroo mother care, peer support and specialised father support, and found they are linked to reduced parental stress, greater parental engagement and efficacy, and better health outcomes for parents.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that structured support for parents during a baby’s NICU stay can matter for family wellbeing, which is useful for anyone wanting to understand how hospitals might help families cope.
ai.life_skill: Notice what support services are available for parents in a neonatal unit and consider using them if you or someone you know is affected.
ai.fact: Six supportive care models for parents of premature infants in NICUs were identified in the review.

quiz.question: How many supportive care models for parents of premature infants in NICUs did the review identify?
quiz.answer: The review identified six possible supportive care models.

ai.caveat: It is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and most of the included studies were rated only moderate quality.

items.title: Effectiveness of Stepped Care Psychological Interventions in Children and Adolescents: A Meta-Analytic Review

ai.headline: Stepped care mental health support for young people works about as well as usual care but costs less.
ai.summary: This preprint reviewed studies of stepped care, where children and adolescents start with lighter support and move to more intensive help only if needed. It found similar mental health outcomes to standard care, including intensive treatments, but significantly lower costs.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how mental health services might help more young people without spending more money.
ai.life_skill: Notice if your mental health support feels too intense or too light, and ask a trusted adult or professional about other options.
ai.fact: About 46% of young people in the reviewed studies moved from the first step of care to a later step.

quiz.question: Did stepped care produce better mental health results than control conditions?
quiz.answer: No, effects compared with control conditions were small and non-significant, meaning outcomes were comparable rather than superior.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings are not final proof.

items.title: Effect of nutrition counseling on complementary feeding practices among mothers with children aged 6–23 months in West Gojjam Zone, Northwest Ethiopia: A cluster-randomized controlled trial

ai.headline: Nutrition counseling helped Ethiopian mothers feed young children more appropriately.
ai.summary: A cluster-randomised trial in rural Northwest Ethiopia compared mothers who received monthly Health Belief Model-based nutrition counseling with mothers who received routine education. Counselled mothers were nearly 2.5 times more likely to practice appropriate complementary feeding, and their children were more likely to meet dietary diversity, meal frequency, and acceptable diet targets.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that structured counseling can improve how young children are fed in similar rural communities, supporting child growth and development.
ai.life_skill: Try asking a qualified health worker or nutritionist for practical advice on what and how often to feed a child aged 6–23 months.
ai.fact: Appropriate complementary feeding is essential for children’s growth and cognitive development.

quiz.question: What did the study find about mothers who received nutrition counseling compared with those who received routine education?
quiz.answer: They were nearly 2.5 times more likely to practice appropriate complementary feeding.

ai.caveat: The results come from one trial in rural Northwest Ethiopia, so they may not apply to other settings.

items.title: Advance Care Planning Impact on the Consistency of Older Adults With Lung Cancer and Their Potential Surrogates Regarding Life-Sustaining Treatment Preferences

ai.headline: A tabletop game helped older adults with lung cancer and their chosen surrogates agree more on life-sustaining treatment choices than a standard manual.
ai.summary: This randomised trial compared an advance care planning tabletop game called “Walking with Wishes” with a standard advance care planning manual in patient–surrogate pairs. The game reduced the gap between patients’ and surrogates’ preferences for five life-sustaining treatments across nine health scenarios, and did not increase state anxiety for either group.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows a simple, low-cost activity can help families understand each other’s wishes about serious medical treatment before a crisis happens.
ai.life_skill: Try talking with a trusted friend or relative about what medical treatments you would or would not want if you became seriously ill.
ai.fact: Advance care planning is the process of discussing and recording preferences for future medical care.
ai.caveat: This is a single trial posted as results on a clinical trials register, so the findings should be treated as preliminary until fully published and peer reviewed.

items.title: The Price of a Chance in Artificial Societies

ai.headline: Reward design changes how simulated agents compete and how much they spend chasing prizes.
ai.summary: Researchers simulated 200 LLM agents competing over 50 rounds to maximise wealth. At low rewards agents invested little, while at high rewards they overcompeted, especially when prize coverage was intermediate. Smaller prizes spread across more winners reduced investment while keeping selection quality similar, but broader coverage lowered selection quality.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how prize structures can shape competition and the costs people bear chasing uncertain rewards.
ai.life_skill: Notice how the size and spread of a prize affects how much effort you are willing to put in.
ai.fact: Agents near the qualification cutoff can invest heavily yet receive no prize and finish poorer than non-winners who invest less.

quiz.question: What happened when smaller prizes were offered to more winners?
quiz.answer: Investment reduced while selection quality was preserved relative to the corresponding top-ability target.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint simulation of artificial LLM agents, not peer-reviewed evidence about real people.

items.title: Sex differences in latent inhibition and their implications for psychotic disorders

ai.headline: Research suggests sex differences in latent inhibition may be linked to psychosis risk, but evidence is mixed.
ai.summary: This systematic review examined studies of latent inhibition in humans and rodents. It found mostly inconclusive evidence for sex differences, though differences were more likely when factors such as drug treatment, juvenile handling, or oestrous phase were involved. New rodent data also suggest sex differences in hippocampal processing during latent inhibition.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain how biological sex might influence learning processes linked to hallucinations and delusions in psychosis.
ai.life_skill: Notice how prior exposure to a harmless cue can reduce your attention to it later, and consider whether stress or other factors change that effect for you.
ai.fact: Latent inhibition is the reduced ability to learn about a stimulus after prior exposure to it without consequence.

quiz.question: What did the systematic review find about sex differences in latent inhibition?
quiz.answer: Evidence was predominantly inconclusive and conflicting, with stronger indications of sex differences when additional factors such as drug administration, juvenile handling, or oestrous phase were studied.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the underlying evidence is described as mostly inconclusive and conflicting.

items.title: Socio-occupational factors and problematic internet use: indirect associations involving negative affect and impulsivity in a predominantly urban, highly educated Romanian adult sample

ai.headline: Lower social support and work engagement, plus higher work addiction, link to problematic internet use via negative mood and impulsivity.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed 215 mostly urban, highly educated Romanian adults about internet use, mood, impulsivity, and work factors. Problematic internet use was linked to less perceived social support and work engagement, and more work addiction, anxiety, depression, and impulsivity; negative mood appeared to be a key indirect pathway.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how workplace wellbeing and emotional state may be connected to unhealthy internet habits in adults.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether low mood or work stress makes you use the internet more than you intend.
ai.fact: Problematic internet use was positively associated with work addiction, depressive symptoms, trait anxiety, and impulsivity.

quiz.question: What did the study find about impulsivity alone as a pathway to problematic internet use?
quiz.answer: The indirect association through impulsivity alone was not significant.

ai.caveat: It was a cross-sectional survey, so it cannot show cause and effect or the order in which things happened.

items.title: EPSBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Earnings Forecasting

ai.headline: AI agents can match analyst earnings forecasts but their confidence intervals are often too narrow.
ai.summary: The study tested six AI models on forecasting US company earnings using filings, transcripts and news. Three models were no worse than analyst consensus, while three made larger errors. Across all models, their stated 80% prediction intervals captured actual earnings only 37% to 70% of the time, mostly because forecasts were too low.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that AI tools for financial forecasting may look reasonable on average but can still be overconfident about how uncertain their predictions are.
ai.life_skill: Treat any AI earnings forecast as uncertain and check whether it gives a realistic range rather than a single number.
ai.fact: EPSBench evaluates AI earnings forecasts across 149 firm-quarters from 86 US companies.

quiz.question: How often did the AI models' stated 80% prediction intervals contain the actual reported EPS?
quiz.answer: Only 37% to 70% of the runs that returned an interval, with most misses above the upper bound because forecasts ran low.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and tests only six models on a fixed set of US firm-quarters, so the results may not generalise.

items.title: Type 2 diabetes breakthrough as 54% achieve remission in just 6 months

ai.headline: A low-calorie diet and exercise program helped 54% of younger adults with type 2 diabetes achieve remission in six months.
ai.summary: Researchers studied younger adults with type 2 diabetes who followed an intensive low-calorie diet and structured exercise program. After six months, 54% achieved remission, compared with 4% who received usual care.
ai.why_it_matters: This shows that lifestyle changes may help some younger adults put type 2 diabetes into remission relatively quickly.
ai.life_skill: Talk to a qualified healthcare professional before making major changes to your diet or exercise routine if you have type 2 diabetes.
ai.fact: 54% of participants under age 45 in the intensive program achieved remission compared with 4% receiving usual care.

quiz.question: What percentage of younger adults in the intensive diet and exercise program achieved remission after six months?
quiz.answer: 54% achieved remission, compared with 4% receiving usual care.

ai.caveat: This is a news report, not the full peer-reviewed study, so the findings cannot yet be treated as proven.

items.title: How one of the body's own proteins drives the vicious cycle of inflammation in vaginal yeast infections

ai.headline: A body protein called albumin drives inflammation in vaginal yeast infections while protecting the fungus from immune attack.
ai.summary: The study looked at why immune responses to Candida albicans yeast infections can be intense and persistent. Researchers found that the host protein albumin fuels the inflammatory cascade and at the same time shields the fungal pathogen from the immune system.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain why thrush symptoms can be severe and keep coming back, pointing toward new ways to treat recurrent infections.
ai.life_skill: If you keep getting thrush symptoms, see a GP or sexual health clinic rather than repeatedly treating yourself.
ai.fact: Up to three-quarters of women will experience a genital yeast infection at least once in their lives.

quiz.question: What does albumin do in vaginal yeast infections according to the study?
quiz.answer: It fuels the inflammatory cascade while shielding the fungal pathogen from the immune system.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about a single study, not peer-reviewed evidence or proof that changing albumin will treat infections.

items.title: Crop diversification protects fields from extreme weather and boosts productivity

ai.headline: Diversifying crops and keeping soil covered helps farms survive extreme weather and produce more food.
ai.summary: Researchers in Brazil tested how varying crop rotations and maintaining constant soil vegetation affect farm resilience. They found these practices help protect crops from droughts and floods while also increasing overall productivity.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding how farming methods can adapt to climate extremes helps explain how global food systems might stay stable in a changing world.
ai.life_skill: Notice how variety in your own routines or projects can make you more resilient to unexpected setbacks.
ai.fact: Keeping soil covered with vegetation is linked to better protection against both droughts and floods.

quiz.question: What two weather events does the study say these farming techniques help protect against?
quiz.answer: The techniques help protect crops against droughts and floods.

ai.caveat: This is a news report summarising a specific regional study, so the results may not apply to all climates or farming systems.

items.title: The asteroid killed the dinosaurs. Why did crocodiles survive?

ai.headline: Crocodiles likely survived the dinosaur-extinction asteroid by staying in warm tropical refuges.
ai.summary: Scientists analysed fossils and ancient climate data to investigate why crocodiles survived the mass extinction event 66 million years ago. The findings suggest that their preference for warm environments kept them in tropical areas that remained habitable after the impact.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how specific environmental preferences can help species survive catastrophic global changes, offering insight into how life adapts to extreme shifts.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your own habits or preferences might help you cope with sudden changes in your environment.
ai.fact: Crocodiles are believed to have survived the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction by inhabiting tropical refuges that remained habitable.

quiz.question: Why did crocodiles survive the asteroid impact according to this analysis?
quiz.answer: Their preference for warm environments placed them in tropical refuges that remained habitable.

ai.caveat: This is a news report summarising a scientific analysis, not a peer-reviewed study itself, so the specific mechanisms are presented as a likely explanation rather than proven fact.

items.title: Oxytocin neurons signal state-dependent transitions from rest to thermogenesis and behavioral arousal

ai.headline: Oxytocin-linked brain cells help mice move from rest to warmth and activity.
ai.summary: Scientists studied oxytocin neurons in the hypothalamus of mice. These neurons became active as mice moved from rest to heat production and alertness, in both social and non-social settings. Stimulating the neurons caused warming followed by increased activity.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain how the brain may link body temperature control with waking up and becoming active.
ai.life_skill: Try noticing whether you feel slightly warmer just before you become more alert after resting.
ai.fact: Oxytocin neurons in the mouse hypothalamus are linked to transitions from rest to heat production and behavioural arousal.

quiz.question: What happened when researchers stimulated oxytocin neurons in resting mice?
quiz.answer: Heat production increased, followed by behavioural arousal.

ai.caveat: The research was conducted in mice, so it cannot be assumed to apply to humans.

items.title: Strategic Monetary Policy in Open Economies -- by Louphou Coulibaly, Charles Engel

ai.headline: Countries setting their own monetary policy can reach the same outcome as cooperating, but only with full commitment.
ai.summary: The paper studies how two countries should set monetary policy when each government acts only in its own interest. It finds that if policymakers can fully commit in advance, acting alone leads to the same result as cooperating, because financial market prices cancel out any benefit from trying to change trade terms. If commitment is only partial, countries end up worse off.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how a country's interest-rate choices can affect other countries through exchange rates and global financial markets, even when each country only looks after itself.
ai.fact: In this model, changes in financial asset prices remove any advantage a country might gain by using monetary policy to improve its trade terms.

quiz.question: What happens to welfare when countries can only make a partial policy commitment?
quiz.answer: The resulting Nash equilibrium yields lower welfare.

ai.caveat: It is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the findings come from a specific theoretical model rather than real-world evidence.

items.title: A New Map of ‘Empty’ Space Challenges a Tranquil Picture of the Galaxy

ai.headline: Astronomers are using 3D maps to show that the space between stars is dynamic, not static.
ai.summary: Astronomers have long treated the interstellar medium as a static backdrop to the universe. New 3D mapping is revealing that the space between stars is dynamic. This challenges the old picture of a tranquil galaxy.
ai.why_it_matters: It changes our picture of the galaxy by showing that even seemingly empty space is active and changing.
ai.fact: The interstellar medium between stars is dynamic rather than a static backdrop.

quiz.question: What did astronomers traditionally treat the interstellar medium as?
quiz.answer: They treated it as a static backdrop to the goings-on of the universe.

ai.caveat: This is a news summary rather than the original research, so it gives no details about the study’s methods or evidence.

items.title: Rewilding project aims to restore peatland

ai.headline: Cumbria Wildlife Trust has begun repairing damaged peatland at Skiddaw Forest.
ai.summary: Cumbria Wildlife Trust has started work to repair damage to peatland at Skiddaw Forest. The project is described as a rewilding effort to restore the area. The announcement does not yet report any results from the work.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how conservation groups begin practical work to repair damaged natural areas.
ai.fact: Wildlife trusts carry out rewilding projects to restore damaged peatland.

quiz.question: Who started work to repair peatland at Skiddaw Forest?
quiz.answer: Cumbria Wildlife Trust started the work.

items.title: Bones may release proteins that slow aging and extend life span

ai.headline: Bones release anti-aging proteins
ai.summary: Researchers studied the effect of exercise on bone cells in mice, finding that exercise triggers the release of anti-aging chemicals. The study focused on osteocytes, a type of bone cell. The findings suggest a potential link between bone health and aging.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding how bones contribute to aging could lead to new strategies for promoting healthy aging and extending lifespan.
ai.life_skill: Try regular exercise to support bone health.
ai.fact: Exercise can trigger the release of anti-aging proteins from bone cells in mice.

quiz.question: What type of cells release anti-aging chemicals in response to exercise?
quiz.answer: Osteocytes release anti-aging chemicals in response to exercise.

ai.caveat: The study was conducted in mice and may not be directly applicable to humans.

items.title: Q&A: Hey AI, who should I vote for this year?

ai.headline: MIT researchers are tracking how AI chatbots answer questions about the 2026 U.S. midterm elections.
ai.summary: MIT professors Adam Berinsky and Chara Podimata have launched a project to monitor AI chatbot responses to election-related queries. The study aims to understand how these tools handle political questions during the 2026 U.S. midterm cycle.
ai.why_it_matters: As people increasingly use AI for information, understanding how these tools frame political topics is crucial for making informed decisions.
ai.life_skill: Check if an AI chatbot provides balanced sources when asking about political events.
ai.fact: AI chatbots are being systematically tracked for their responses to specific election questions.

quiz.question: What is the main goal of the MIT project described?
quiz.answer: To track how AI chatbots respond to questions about the 2026 U.S. midterm elections.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about a new project, not a completed study with final results or conclusions.

items.title: Comparison and effects of coordination based circuit training and small side games on agility and dynamic balance in healthy students aged 15-18 years
items.venue: Pedagogy of Physical Culture and Sports

ai.headline: Structured circuit training improves dynamic balance more than small-sided games in teenagers.
ai.summary: This randomised trial compared coordination-based circuit training, small-sided games, and regular school activity in 84 students aged 15–18. Both training types improved agility and dynamic balance compared to the control group, but circuit training produced significantly better dynamic balance scores than small-sided games.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding which type of exercise targets specific motor skills helps young people choose activities that support better movement control and injury prevention.
ai.life_skill: Notice that different physical activities target different skills; structured drills may help with balance while games help with agility.
ai.fact: In this study, coordination-based circuit training was more effective than small-sided games for improving dynamic balance in adolescents.

quiz.question: Which intervention was better for improving dynamic balance?
quiz.answer: Coordination-based circuit training produced significantly higher dynamic balance scores than small-sided games.

ai.caveat: The study involved non-athlete students in Indonesia, so results may not apply to elite athletes or other populations.

items.title: Remote supervised exercise- and physical activity-based rehabilitation for post-stroke depression, anxiety, and quality of life: a systematic review, evidence map, and exploratory quantitative synthesis.

ai.headline: Exercise helps post-stroke depression
ai.summary: Researchers studied remote exercise programs for post-stroke depression and anxiety. They found a possible benefit for depression, but the evidence is fragile. The programs often included psychological support, making it hard to isolate the effect of exercise alone.
ai.why_it_matters: This research matters because it could help people recover from strokes and improve their mental health
ai.life_skill: Try incorporating physical activity into your daily routine to improve your mental wellbeing
ai.fact: Remote exercise programs can include a combination of physical activity and psychological support

quiz.question: What type of programs were studied for post-stroke depression and anxiety?
quiz.answer: Remote exercise- and physical activity-based rehabilitation programs

ai.caveat: The evidence is fragile and based on a limited number of studies with complex interventions

items.title: PROBLEMATIC SMARTPHONE USE, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, AND OBESITY RISK IN CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS: A NARRATIVE REVIEW

ai.headline: Problematic smartphone use is linked to lower physical activity and higher obesity risk in young people.
ai.summary: This narrative review examined 45 studies on how problematic smartphone use affects physical activity and weight in children and adolescents. It found associations between heavy phone use, reduced movement, and excess body weight, though the evidence is mixed and mostly observational.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding this link helps young people recognise how screen habits might be quietly replacing active time, which is crucial for long-term health.
ai.life_skill: Notice if you are scrolling instead of moving, and try swapping one hour of screen time for physical activity.
ai.fact: Reducing smartphone use has been associated with increased physical activity in some studies, but this does not prove it prevents obesity.

quiz.question: Did the review prove that using a smartphone causes obesity?
quiz.answer: No, the review found associations but noted that the observational evidence limits causal interpretation.

ai.caveat: The evidence is heterogeneous and predominantly observational, so it cannot establish that smartphone use directly causes obesity.

items.title: Psilocybin, cognitive stability and drinking reduction in co-occurring alcohol use disorder and depression: a pilot secondary analysis of a randomized, placebo-controlled trial

ai.headline: Psilocybin slowed task switching one week after dosing, but did not consistently change other thinking skills or willingness to try hard.
ai.summary: This pilot study looked at people with both alcohol use disorder and depression who took psilocybin or placebo in a randomized trial. About a week later, psilocybin slowed responses in cued task switching, but effects on other thinking measures were inconsistent and none were statistically robust after correction. Drinking fell in both groups and was linked to greater cognitive stability, while depressive symptoms improved more after psilocybin but were not tied to thinking changes.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that early pilot results about psychedelics and thinking should be treated as tentative, not proof, because the study was small and exploratory.

quiz.question: What did the study find about psilocybin and willingness to exert mental effort?
quiz.answer: There was no detectable effect on demand avoidance, which indexed willingness to exert control.

ai.caveat: This is a small pilot secondary analysis of a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, so the findings are preliminary and not proof.

items.title: Characterizing Rejection Sensitivity in Autistic Adolescents and Implications for Depression and Anxiety Symptoms

ai.headline: Feeling anxious about rejection is linked to social anxiety in autistic teens, but not depression.
ai.summary: This preprint surveyed 106 autistic adolescents to look at how rejection sensitivity relates to mental health. It found that while almost all participants experienced some rejection sensitivity, only the anxious type was linked to social anxiety symptoms, not depression or general anxiety.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding that specific feelings of rejection anxiety connect to social anxiety can help young people and support workers identify specific stressors rather than assuming all rejection feelings lead to the same mental health issues.
ai.life_skill: Notice if your fear of rejection feels more like nervousness about social situations or anger, as these may affect your mood differently.
ai.fact: Rejection sensitivity is common in autistic adolescents, with higher rates observed in females and those with stronger autistic traits.

quiz.question: Did the study find that rejection sensitivity predicted depression in autistic adolescents?
quiz.answer: No, the study found that neither anxious nor angry rejection sensitivity predicted depression.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the observational design cannot prove that rejection sensitivity causes social anxiety.

items.title: Toward an Empirical Comparison of Bourdieu and Latour: Relational Theories in the Sociology of Poverty

ai.headline: Resources can help people in poverty while still leaving them dependent and financially insecure.
ai.summary: The study reanalysed twenty respondent files from an archive of 216 registrations collected in three Dutch urban areas. It found that skills could persist while their financial returns changed, contracts and payments could coexist with an inability to start work, and similar purchases could create different obligations toward future income.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows why practical help can improve someone’s situation without removing their ongoing money worries.
ai.life_skill: Check what ongoing costs or obligations come with any resource or payment before you rely on it.
ai.fact: A resource can be usable and valuable while still leaving a person dependent and financially insecure.

quiz.question: What did the study find about similar purchases made by people experiencing poverty?
quiz.answer: Similar purchases could create different obligations towards future income.

ai.caveat: It is a preprint not yet peer reviewed and based on a small, purposively selected set of files from Dutch urban areas.

items.title: Construction of a hierarchical linear regression prediction model for classical Chinese poetry writing ability development

items.title: Problematic media use, but not device time, tracks mental health issues: A four-wave cohort study in adolescents

ai.headline: Problematic media use, not just screen time, is linked to adolescent mental health issues.
ai.summary: This preprint followed 550 Swiss adolescents over two years to compare the effects of device time versus problematic use on mental health. It found that while screen time predicted problematic use, only problematic use—especially of social media—was strongly linked to anxiety, depression, and ADHD symptoms.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that worrying about how many hours you spend on a device is less useful than noticing if you feel unable to control your usage.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether you feel compelled to check your phone or social media even when you want to stop, rather than just counting your hours.
ai.fact: In this study, problematic social media use showed strong reciprocal ties with mental health issues, whereas screen time was only weakly associated.

quiz.question: According to the study, which factor was more strongly linked to mental health issues: total screen time or problematic use?
quiz.answer: Problematic use, particularly of social media, was more strongly linked to mental health issues than total screen time.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and it shows associations rather than proving that problematic use causes mental health problems.

items.title: Crowdstorming You Can Trust? Assessing the Reliability of Crowdsourced Ideation and Prioritization

ai.headline: Different groups of people often come up with similar good ideas when solving the same problem.
ai.summary: Researchers asked two separate groups of MBA students to independently suggest and rank ways to improve their course. They found that both groups proposed semantically similar ideas, especially the valuable ones, and prioritised them in a similar order.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that collective decision-making can be more consistent and reliable than people usually assume, even without everyone talking to each other.
ai.life_skill: Notice that when you ask different friends for advice on the same problem, their best suggestions often overlap.
ai.fact: In this study, two independent groups converged on similar high-quality ideas while diverging on poor ones.

quiz.answer: The groups showed convergence among valuable ideas and divergence among poor ones.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint based on a single exploratory study with one specific group of students, so it is not yet peer-reviewed proof.

items.title: Personalized and differentially private federated learning for mobility data mining via the TrajectoryGuard framework

ai.headline: A new framework lets devices train mobility models together without sharing raw GPS data, keeping location traces private.
ai.summary: The study tested TrajectoryGuard, a privacy-preserving federated learning system that keeps raw location traces such as GPS logs on users' devices while using differential privacy and secure aggregation to train models. On the GeoLife and T-Drive Beijing taxi datasets, it reached 92.5% accuracy for predicting destination categories and cut communication overhead by 30% per round, with a privacy guarantee of ε = 0.9 at σ² = 1.0.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how cities and apps could analyse movement patterns for transport planning without collecting people's actual location histories.
ai.life_skill: Check an app's privacy settings to see whether it shares your raw location data or only processed insights.
ai.fact: Federated learning trains models across many devices without centralising raw user data.

quiz.question: What did TrajectoryGuard predict from partial GPS trajectories?
quiz.answer: It predicted a destination category such as home, workplace, or shopping location.

ai.caveat: The results come from experiments on specific datasets and a proposed framework, not from real-world deployment across diverse populations.

ai.summary: The study develops and tests an intervention for parents of children with behavioural insomnia of childhood. It focuses on helping parents manage their thoughts about their child's sleep.

items.title: Revisiting Over-refusal in Safety-aligned Large Language Models: A Representation and Optimization Perspective

ai.headline: AI safety systems can wrongly block harmless questions, and researchers propose a way to reduce this.
ai.summary: The study examines why safety-aligned large language models sometimes refuse harmless queries that look risky. It finds that harmful and over-refused samples become harder to distinguish in deeper model layers, and that harmful-sample gradients are more aligned with refusal targets than helpful targets on over-refusal prompts. The authors propose a framework called GOAL to reduce over-refusal while keeping safety performance.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain why AI assistants may refuse safe requests, which matters as more people rely on them for everyday information.
ai.life_skill: If an AI refuses a harmless question, try rephrasing it or check with another source before assuming the topic is unsafe.
ai.fact: Safety-aligned large language models can mistakenly reject harmless queries that appear superficially risky.

quiz.question: What did the study find about harmful and over-refusal samples in deeper model layers?
quiz.answer: Their representations increasingly overlap, making it harder for the model to keep a clear boundary between them.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings should be treated as preliminary.

items.title: Transcranial electrical stimulation for memory enhancement: A systematic review and meta-analysis

ai.headline: Brain stimulation is linked to small memory improvements in healthy adults, but effects are short-lived.
ai.summary: This systematic review analysed 193 trials involving over 7,000 healthy adults to see if transcranial electrical stimulation (tES) improves memory. It found a small overall benefit for working and declarative memory compared to fake stimulation, with effects lasting up to one day.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that non-invasive brain stimulation might be a safe tool for boosting cognitive performance, though the gains are modest and temporary.
ai.life_skill: Notice that while technology can offer small cognitive boosts, consistent practice and sleep remain the most reliable ways to support memory.
ai.fact: Tingling and itching on the scalp were more common during active stimulation than during sham sessions, but no serious adverse events were reported.

quiz.question: How long did the memory improvements from stimulation last in this study?
quiz.answer: Significant pooled effects were observed within 1 day after stimulation, while longer-term estimates were imprecise.

ai.caveat: The study is a preprint not yet peer-reviewed, and the authors note that heterogeneity and small-study effects limit conclusions about long-term safety and durability.

items.title: Negative affectivity moderates the association between job demands and hair cortisol in healthcare workers: a cross-sectional multi-method study

ai.headline: Stress from certain job demands may raise long-term stress hormone levels more in people high in negative affectivity.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 67 healthcare workers in Northern Italy, measuring job demands, negative affectivity, and hair cortisol as a marker of long-term stress. Job demands were not linked to cortisol overall, but among people high in negative affectivity, problem solving and time pressure were more strongly linked to higher hair cortisol.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that personality differences can shape how workplace stress affects the body over time.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether time pressure or problem solving at work affects your stress more than it does for others, and consider discussing workload with a supervisor or occupational health professional.
ai.fact: Hair cortisol concentration is used as a biomarker of long-term activation of the body’s stress response system.

quiz.question: What did the study find about job demands and hair cortisol in people high in negative affectivity?
quiz.answer: Among people high in negative affectivity, problem solving and time pressure were more strongly linked to higher hair cortisol.

ai.caveat: This was a small cross-sectional study of 67 workers, so it cannot show that job demands cause changes in cortisol.

items.title: AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers

ai.headline: A new method speeds up AI video generation by skipping most attention calculations while keeping quality high.
ai.summary: The study tested AB-Attention, a training-free technique that approximates full attention in video diffusion transformers by selectively computing only important blocks of data. On two video models, it skipped 89–92% of attention work, improved image quality by up to 4.4 dB over the strongest baseline, and achieved up to 2.23 times faster end-to-end speedup.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI video tools can become faster and more efficient without losing visual quality, which could make them cheaper and more accessible in everyday use.
ai.life_skill: Try using AI video tools that advertise efficient or accelerated generation to save time and computing power.
ai.fact: AB-Attention can skip 89–92% of attention calculations in video diffusion transformers while maintaining or improving quality.

quiz.question: What did AB-Attention achieve compared to baselines in terms of attention computation?
quiz.answer: It skipped 89–92% of attention, whereas baselines computed 1.8–3.6 times as much.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint not yet peer reviewed, and the findings are based on technical experiments with two specific video models rather than real-world user trials.

items.title: A decade of carbon dioxide data from space gets an upgrade

ai.headline: NASA satellites are getting an upgrade to measure carbon dioxide from space more accurately.
ai.summary: Two NASA instruments, OCO-2 and OCO-3, take over a million daily observations of sunlight reflecting off Earth. An algorithm uses the physics of light travelling through air to turn these readings into atmospheric carbon dioxide concentrations.
ai.why_it_matters: Better satellite data helps scientists track where carbon dioxide is coming from and how it moves around the planet.

ai.fact: OCO-2 and OCO-3 capture more than a million observations of sunlight reflecting off Earth's surface every day.

quiz.answer: They capture sunlight reflecting off Earth's surface, which an algorithm converts into atmospheric carbon dioxide concentrations.

items.title: A single brain signal may explain schizophrenia's most puzzling symptoms

ai.headline: A weakened brain signal may link several puzzling symptoms of schizophrenia.
ai.summary: Researchers studied brain signals in people with schizophrenia and found that a weakened signal may connect sensory processing difficulties, disorganized speech, and greater symptom severity. ai.why_it_matters: It offers a possible explanation for why seemingly unrelated symptoms of schizophrenia occur together.
ai.fact: A weakened brain signal may be linked to sensory processing difficulties, disorganized speech, and greater symptom severity in schizophrenia.

quiz.answer: A weakened brain signal may connect sensory processing difficulties, disorganized speech, and greater symptom severity.

items.title: Distinct gradients of cortical architecture capture visual representations and behavior across the lifespan

ai.headline: Two brain architecture gradients map how visual areas are organised and change across life.
ai.summary: Researchers used MRI to study the human visual cortex and found two gradients of cortical structure—one where cell and myelin features converge and another where they diverge. These gradients predict visual brain organisation and new visual representations, and each follows a different pattern across the lifespan.

ai.fact: The visual cortex contains two distinct architectural gradients that relate to visual behaviour and change differently across the lifespan.

ai.caveat: This is a single observational study using MRI, so it shows links rather than proving cause and effect.

items.title: Representation, Innovation, and Product Adoption -- by Jennifer L. Kao, Tamar Oostrom

ai.headline: Paying for elderly people to join drug trials led to more trials and more drug use by older adults.
ai.summary: Researchers studied a 2000 Medicare change that lowered the cost of including elderly people in clinical trials. ai.why_it_matters: It shows how changing who is included in research can change which medicines get developed and who ends up using them.

ai.fact: A policy change that lowered the cost of including elderly participants in clinical trials increased their representation and shifted drug development toward diseases common in older age.

quiz.answer: Trial sponsors included more elderly participants and ran more trials for diseases common among older people, leading to greater drug use by that group.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the findings come from observing a policy change rather than a randomised experiment.
